March 3, 2025
To: Sen. Chip Curry, Representative Traci Gere, and Representative Tiffany Roberts.
My name is Amanda McDaniel and I am the Director of Main Street Bath, happily in my sixth year of this unique role. Main Street Bath is the first accredited Main Street program in the State of Maine, established in 2001. We are looking forward to celebrating our 25th Anniversary in 2026.
This program is an active member promoting the holistic and successful model of the Four Point Approach from the National Main Street America program. Created out of the National Historic Trust, the work of Main Street is to preserve and promote historic downtowns that would otherwise be suffering from a lack of coordinated programming. We hang our hat on creating cohesive collaborative communication between municipal, non profit, business and residential narratives. We are not a membership model, so we can actively serve all within our downtown footprint. We create events that draw in tourism, resources that support small business, and actively maintain a culture of welcome and belonging for our downtown community.
There was a time in which Bath, and many other downtowns that have become accredited or affiliate Main Street Programs, was in a troubled time, without advocacy, without planning, without partnership to move forward. These historic downtowns have properties that are crumbling, with outdated systems and could very easily be bulldozed to be turned into cheaper, less attractive strip malls. Our work aims to provide as much assistance, resiliency, ideas, and vibrancy to prevent us from losing the character, feeling and atmosphere our historic downtowns offer.  We would not be able to act as a Main Street, or be connected to the National Main Street America programming without having a state level agency to assist, guide, connect and convene us. This state level advocacy is the Maine Downtown Center. All of the 841+ accredited Main Street Programs across the nation all have a State Coordinating Program above them. This is the only way we can successfully operate.  The economic and tourism impact of the loss of Main Street Programs to our downtowns would be extreme. The municipalities and chambers do not have the bandwidth for the depth of on-the-street programming we provide. You can say goodbye to Bath Heritage Days, Old Fashioned Christmas in Bath, all the Free Summer Concert Series and the only tourism that Bath offers, with www.visitbath.com, the Bath Regional Information Center and the 25,000 annual copies of Map of Bath. This is only a small pie slice of the year round work plan we have in operation.  Please support LD 629, so that Maine Development Foundation's Maine Downtown Center can exist, so in turn, we can exist. Our partnership is essential, required, and a true sense of advocacy for what keeps Maine feeling the way it should be.
Best, Amanda McDaniel Director of Main Street Bath 15 Commercial Street, Bath, Maine 04350 (207) 350-7775 or (207) 442-7291 director@visitbath.com www.visitbath.com

Dear Senator Chip Curry, Senate Chair and Representative Traci Gere, House Chair, Committee on Housing and Economic Development and Representative Tiffany Roberts,
I am writing to express my strong support for LD 629 and to urge you to restore funding for the Maine Development Foundation (MDF). As Executive Director of Saco Main Street, I have personally experienced the invaluable impact of MDF's programs, particularly through the Maine Downtown Center (MDC). Their expertise and support have been instrumental in strengthening our downtown, driving economic development, and fostering vibrant communities across the state.
When the Maine Legislature established MDF over 40 years ago, it recognized the importance of investing in statewide economic and community development. However, over time, state funding for MDF disappeared, despite the organization continuing to provide critical services. LD 629 seeks to restore this funding--adjusted for inflation to $500,000--ensuring that MDF can continue its vital work supporting Maine communities.
The impact of MDF's work is undeniable. Through MDC, they serve as the only statewide resource dedicated to downtown revitalization, filling a gap in expertise that no other organization in Maine provides. The demand for their services continues to grow, and their individualized approach leads to proven success. For every $1 invested in one of Maine's 11 Main Street communities, there is a remarkable $23 return--demonstrating the power of strategic, local investment.
I have seen firsthand how MDC's support leads to tangible results. Through their initiatives, we successfully secured an Entrepreneur Ecosystem grant that not only benefited the businesses in our downtown but also provided the opportunity to build a stronger relationship with our neighboring Main Street, Heart of Biddeford. MDC's annual accreditation visits also help communities like ours stay on track and continuously improve our impact.
I strongly encourage you to support LD 629 and restore the funding that was always intended to support MDF's work. This investment will ensure Maine's downtowns and communities continue to thrive for generations to come.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I appreciate your leadership and commitment to strengthening Maine's communities.
Sincerely,
Angie Presby Executive Director, Saco Main Street

10036000:
March 5, 2025
Dear Sen. Chip Curry, Senate Chair and Rep. Traci Gere, House Chair, Committee on Housing and Economic Development and the Sponsor is Representative Tiffany Roberts:
I am writing to express Heart of Biddeford's strong support for "An Act to Restore Matching Funding to the Maine Development Foundation LD 629." The impact of the Maine Development Foundation (MDF) and its Maine Downtown Center (MDC) program are evident across our state, and its work has been instrumental in the revitalization and ongoing success of Biddeford's downtown and mill district.
A striking example of the effectiveness of this network occurred this past year when the Maine Downtown Center conference was held in Biddeford. During lunchtime, 160 conference participants were set to eat at 16 different downtown restaurants. However, just before noon, a local construction incident struck a transformer, cutting power to all of these businesses. Despite this unexpected challenge, the response was immediate and seamless. The Maine Downtown Center, along with hosts from Heart of Biddeford and Saco Main Street, sprang into action, contacting each restaurant to determine who could continue serving with cold foods. Within 80 minutes, all participants were successfully fed, and the conference continued without missing a beat.
While this may seem like a story about one unique incident, it is, in fact, a metaphor for the essential role of the MDF/MDC. It highlights what is possible when a small, dedicated group of individuals--skilled in communication, adaptability, and collaboration--comes together to problem-solve and sustain momentum toward shared goals. These skills are precisely what the Maine Development Foundation cultivates through its programs, and they are more necessary than ever in a time of economic uncertainty, social divisions, and environmental challenges.
Heart of Biddeford's mission is to foster a vibrant, inclusive, and sustainable downtown, and the Maine Downtown Center has played a vital role in supporting this mission. The Main Street program provides communities with the tools and training necessary to sustain and grow, and Biddeford's ongoing revitalization is a testament to the power of this work. Since we were awarded the Great American Main Street Award in 2022, our city has become a national model for downtown redevelopment, attracting visitors and inquiries from across the country about how we've achieved this success. The foundation of this transformation can be traced back to the support, guidance, and strategies provided by MDF/MDC.
This past year, Heart of Biddeford applied for a $20 million EPA grant in collaboration with the University of New England. This rigorous five-month process was a major undertaking, and while we were not among the 4% of applicants selected, the experience built invaluable skills and partnerships that will serve us in future opportunities. The confidence and expertise to take on such a challenge is directly attributed to the training, high-bar and leadership we have received from the Maine Downtown Center.
The work of MDF/MDC goes far beyond one community--it is a statewide force for

economic and community development. It has helped foster entrepreneurship, attract investment, and create thriving downtowns that serve as economic and cultural hubs for our state. Without their guidance, many of Maine's historic downtowns would struggle to define and sustain themselves. Instead, under their leadership, communities are flourishing and sustaining. We urge you to restore the $500,000 in funding that was the intent of the legislature when MDF was originally started. This amount is adjusted for inflation from the original amount in 1978. The return on investment for their work is exponential, and their continued support is critical to sustaining Maine's economic vitality. Please do not hesitate to reach out with any questions. Sincerely,
 Delilah Poupore Executive Director
Mission Statement: Powered by the strength of community involvement, Heart of Biddeford fosters a vibrant, inclusive and sustainable
downtown for residents, businesses, and visitors.

RE: Support of LD 629
Dear Senator Chip Curry, Senate Chair and Representative Traci Gere, House Chair of the Committee on Housing and Economic Development and Sponsor of LD 629, Representative Tiffany Roberts:
My name is Eric (EJ) Roach, and I am the Director of Economic & Community Development for the City of Old Town. I also live in Old Town, along with 7,500 other folks. These 7,500 residents may not be aware of the Maine Development Foundation, the Maine Downtown Center, or even the Institute for Civic Leadership. However, these programs and resources offered by MDF have directly impacted the community where they live and work. Located on the banks of the Penobscot river, Old Town has held a close relationship with its surrounding waters, and has a rich history of log drives, water powered sawmills, canoe building, and pulp and paper manufacturing. If you live in a community with a pulp & paper mill you deal with uncertainty. When I spoke to this committee last year, the paper mill in Old Town was idle. As I submit this testimony, it remains idle. Our current uncertainty, coupled with decades of uncertainty makes supporting MDF and our ongoing relationship even more important.
I am asking for your support of LD 629 so MDF can continue to provide its high-quality programs and services such as the Maine Downtown Center and the Institute for Civic Leadership.
Maine Downtown Center
The City of Old Town has directly benefited from the Maine Downtown Center and their guidance helping us focus on our downtown redevelopment. The following are key items that outline our engagement and support from MDF/MDC as it relates to our Downtown.
�MDF's Maine Downtown Center staff visited Old Town initially as part of the FOR ME program to meet with municipal staff and elected officials to discuss what a formal downtown revitalization program looked like and to put eyes on our downtown and see it first-hand.
�We received a small mini grant to complete a downtown project so the community would start thinking more about downtown and how small incremental steps can make an impact.
�We received consulting services for a community engagement process called the Downtown Revitalization Roadmap process which gave the community a path forward and outlined priorities for our downtown revitalization efforts.
�The Maine Downtown Center Staff spent a great deal of time working with City staff and a local volunteer committee on developing a downtown focused organization.
�When the FOR Maine effort concluded, the Maine Downtown Center continued to support Old Town by regularly attending meetings and assisting with the launch of our organization. They provided best practices from other communities around Maine and nationally so that we did not have to reinvent the wheel.

�Downtown Old Town, with the help of the Maine Downtown Center, became an official MDC Affiliate Community February 1, 2024.
�Downtown Old Town, one year later was selected to host the Maine Downtown Center Affiliate Jamboree, scheduled for Friday March 7, 2025.
Old Town has been talking about developing our downtown for decades. We had the passion and vision, but we were missing something. What we were missing was a framework to focus our initiatives and a friend to help show us the way. We needed a framework that focuses on Economic Vitality, Design, Organization, and Promotion. The Main Downtown Center has brought this Maine Street America approach to Old Town and has been that "friend" to help us get there.
Institute for Civic Learning
I am a graduate of the Institute for Civic Leadership (Elephant Class) of MDF. I eagerly became a participant after two staff members, our Assistant City Manager and our Finance Director participated. As our assistant City Manager often says, "ICL is the best thing since sliced bread"! Our Library Director is a current ICL participant, and we are in the process of recruiting participants for this year's class. You may recognize a pattern of our support and engagement with MDF and their leadership programs.
The ICL experience was transformative to say the least. I learned how to not only be a better leader for Old Town, but it made me a better person. The connections I made with other leaders at ICL have continued beyond ICL. Over a year has passed since the program concluded and we continue to support each other and collaborate on projects and initiatives across the entire State of Maine.
Although I am one of a few Old Town leaders to experience ICL, my 7,500 neighbors in Old Town have indirectly benefited from our involvement in the program.
I would kindly remined you when the legislature created MDF over 40 years ago the legislature gave MDF funding for the work MDF was doing for the State of Maine. Somewhere along the way that funding disappeared. I strongly encourage you to restore the $500,000 in funding that was the intent of the legislature when MDF was originally started. This $500,000 is adjusted for inflation from the original amount in 1978.
MDC's impact is great. They serve as a statewide resource for downtown revitalization. Their successful engagement has led to an increased demand for their services. They fill a gap in knowledge and services that no one else is doing in the State of Maine. Their individualized approach takes more time but has great impact and satisfaction and success at the local level. The return on investment continues to be that for every $1 invested in one of Maine's 11 Main Streets, there is a $23 return on that investment.
I thank you for your support of LD 629.
Eric "E.J." Roach
City of Old Town

Patrick Strauch, Executive Director

Good afternoon, Senator Curry, Representative Gere and members of the Committee on Housing and Economic
Development. I'm Patrick Strauch of Exeter, Maine. I'm here testifying today as the Executive Director of the
Maine Forest Products Council. The Maine Forest Products Council is an organization representing more than 300 members from all facets of the forest products industry from the stump to the mill. Our members include
paper mills, sawmills, secondary wood processors and large landowners. Our membership also includes banks
and insurance companies. We represent anyone with an interest in promoting a robust and healthy forest prod-
ucts industry.
I am here today to testify in support of LD 629, "An Act to Restore matching Funding to the Maine Develop-
ment Foundation" by the sponsor, Representative Roberts. For the last eight years, the Maine Forest Products Council has worked collaboratively with the Maine Development Foundation on a unique cross-sector collaboration called the Forest Opportunity Roadmap, also known as FOR/Maine. This project brings together industry, communities, govermnent, institutions of higher education and non-profits to help Maine strategically adapt and capitalize on changing markets to maintain our leading role in the global forest economy. Since its inception eight years ago, the Council has helped lead this effort, which is staffed by the Maine Development Foundation. This ongoing effort has been tremendously successful, and that is in part thanks to the good, credible, non-partisan work of the Maine Development Foundation. The Maine Development Foundation has been a great organization to partner with.
MDF is uniquely valuable, the support they've provided to not only the whole effort but the deep working rela-
tionship we've been able to forge with our work force committee chaired by Ryan Bushy with Louisiana Pacific
as it works on DOL credentialing issues and educational curriculum in Maine's K-12 school systems. There are
also important efforts to work with distressed mill towns to craft efforts to enable their comeback. I also believe
MDF involvement in the FOR/Maine project has strengthened their knowledge of natural resource issues that
are a critical part of Maine's heritage and future opportunity.

These efforts have been important to the forest industry, and they need to be persistent and sustainable. I've
seen firsthand how during the startup phases and the transitions between competitive grants (valleys of death),
MDF seeks with the partners to lean in as best they to support these communities. More core support is justi-
fied.
LD 262, provides ongoing funds to restore matching funds for private contributions to support MDF's eco-
nomic, workforce and community development initiatives. These funds, which would help MDF leverage up to
$500,000 per year, would allow the organization to continue its great work, which are of a great benefit to our economy and state.
For these reasons, please vote `Ought to pass' on LD 629. I would be happy to answer any questions that you
may have.

Dear Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and Honorable Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Housing and Economic Development:
My name is Sarah Hansen, and I am writing to offer my enthusiastic support of An Act to Restore Matching Funding to the Maine Development Foundation (LD 629).
Back in 1977, the State of Maine pledged to support the Maine Development Foundation annually by matching the first $250,000 in private sector funding. Unfortunately, the state has not followed through with this commitment since the early 1990s, and MDF is making do with an allocation of only $58,000. As a state-chartered public-private partnership - structured deliberately to be independent, not a state agency - MDF is unique in its ability to be entrepreneurial and innovative. They have become strong economic champions of Maine's economy, creating dynamic and transformational opportunities for all communities and economic sectors throughout the state. It is time for the state to renew their commitment and restore the $250,000 to support MDF's invaluable leadership.
The Maine Downtown Center (MDC), one of MDF's leading programs, has made an invaluable impact on communities across Maine. They serve as a statewide resource for downtown revitalization, and the demand for services continues to rise. MDC fills a gap in knowledge and services that no one else is able to provide. Their individualized approach takes more time, but has great impact and satisfaction and success at the local level. The return on investment continues to be overwhelming: for every $1 invested in one of Maine's 11 Main Streets, there is a $23 return.
MDF's track record is proven and makes clear the return on investment will be substantial. They continue to leverage their unrestricted funds to maximize impact for the State of Maine. My own personal experience as an Advisory Council Member for the Maine Downtown Center has allowed me to see the extraordinary impact of MDF first-hand. Please support the incredible work of the Maine Development Foundation by honoring the matching fund commitment made back in 1977.
Please support An Act to Restore Matching Funding to the Maine Development Foundation (LD 629). Thank you very much for your consideration.
Sincerely,
Sarah Hansen Westbrook, Maine

Good morning Senator Curry, Representative Gere and distinguished members of the Housing
and Economic Development Committee. My name is Tiffany Roberts, and I have the honor of
representing House District 149, which includes the communities of North Berwick and South
Berwick. I come before you today to present LD 629, An Act to Restore Matching Funding to
the Maine Development Foundation.
The purpose of this legislation is to amplify the impact of a vital public-private partnership -- the
Maine Development Foundation (MDF). MDF plays a pivotal role in addressing Maine's
workforce challenges and contributes significantly to economic and community development.
MDF's efforts with initiatives like the Forest Opportunity Roadmap and the SEAMaine address innovative pathways to prosperity. Importantly, MDF's statewide reach is invaluable to smaller
service centers and rural regions, providing access to expertise and programming.
LD 629 appropriates General Fund support of $500,000 per year to MDF to expand and sustain
the impact of its programming and fulfill the pledge that the legislature made in 1977 and kept
until 1991. I believe that we have bipartisan agreement on the value that MDF provides and see
the potentially significant impact that would be available with this funding. Although one legislature cannot bind another, let us stay true to the original commitment.
Defining this funding as general program support enables it to go where it is most needed to match other funding, bridge other funding and ensure that efforts can be persistent and powerful in reaching more communities and meeting the needs of economic and workforce development for economic growth.
Currently, MDF receives a small amount of General Fund support each year of just over $58,000 which is earmarked for specific initiatives. They also are a contractor to DECD for the Growth

Council for about $90,000 per year. This is out of their budget of over $3 million, where less
than 5% comes from the state.

partnership with $250,000 in annual state matching funds. (The proposed $500,000 only partially
accounts for decades of inflation -- full inflation would bring it to $1.3 million per year!) And let's help ensure critical Work doesn't wither on the vine when short-term outside grants come
and go. MDF has been able to win many competitive federal grants, but their important work in
Maine must persist even when there is uncertainty about the funding outlook in DC.

leveraged their independence, private sector relationships and entrepreneurial grant-writing for this important public mission, even absent our original pledge. Imagine what could be done if that was restored.
This legislation will sustain and enhance MDF's critical impact on our workforce, economy and
communities.

Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and Honorable Members,
The Maine Development Foundation (MDF) offers testimony, via our CEO Yellow Light Breen of Holden,
Maine, in support of the proposed legislation to restore $500,000 in state matching funding to MDF. This
provision honors an original cormnitment dating back to our founding in 1977, largely neglected since the early 1990s, and only partially updated for decades of inflation.
MDF is a statewide non-profit, non-partisan membership organization uniquely established by the Legislature
and the Governor in 1977 to work across the business, government, nonprofit, and education sectors on long-
range strategies for growing Maine's economy. We do this through our trusted economic research, leadership
programs, and several signature public-private partnerships.
This Committee is hopefully now familiar with some of our valuable programming: the nonpartisan
Measures of Growth annual scorecard on the Maine economy; our leadership development programs including the Policy Leaders Academy "bus tours" for the Legislature; and our cross-sector partnerships such
as the Maine Downtown Center, Forest Opportunity Roadmap for Maine (FOR/Maine), and SEAMaine.
Restored match funding will not only Fulfill Commitments, but it will also Leverage Opportunities, Drive Impact, and Maintain Services in uncertain times.
Investing $500,000 each year would enable MDF's to maintain essential core activities in economic
development, workforce development, and downtown revitalization and to continue to meet critical increased
need, particularly for communities, industries, and individuals that are most-often underserved, economically
distressed, both rural and urban. We would hope to leverage the State's investment 2X over the long term.
This would achieve in part the long-neglected promise of the State dating back to 1977 to match the first
$250,000 of private sector contributions (in 1977 dollars -- let alone with decades of inflation, approximately
$1.3 million in today's dollarsl). Currently, MDF receives only small portions of dedicated funding for
specific purposes and projects (including a contract for Measures of Growth) but the grand total is less than
$150,000 or less than 5% of MDF's budget. We have leveraged the State General Ftmd investment 20X over.
Without matching investment, MDF is heavily dependent on limited-period, limited-purpose competitive
federal grants. Just last month, one already-awarded $1.5 million federal grant to serve economically distressed areas of central and western Maine was arbitrarily terminated.
What Can We Do with Your Investment -- What Additional Impact Can MDF Have?
Why not simply continue on with MDF's disproportionate but often successful reliance on competitive,
episodic project grants from private and federal sources`? Grants typically require match and are on a
discontinuous timeline. They often cannot be renewed. Many funders want to fund the startup phase but not
the ongoing work. Most grants cannot be used to fund the grant-writing efforts for pursuit of complementary funds. And, as we have learned --funders can change investment priorities quickly. Thus, matching funds,
